name: Unstable angina
rawContent:
# Unstable angina: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
Unstable angina is myocardial ischaemia at rest or with minimal exertion without persistent troponin elevation, and is part of acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

overview.definition: Unstable angina is myocardial ischaemia at rest or with minimal exertion without persistent troponin elevation, and is part of acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
overview.epidemiology: Common emergency presentation in adults with cardiovascular risk factors.
overview.pathophysiology: Usually due to plaque disruption with non-occlusive thrombus causing dynamic coronary obstruction.

symptoms: Chest pain at rest or crescendo pattern
atypicalPresentations: Epigastric discomfort, dyspnoea alone, especially in older people/diabetes

secondLine: Risk stratification (e.g. GRACE) and early cardiology review

diagnosis.criteria: Clinical ACS symptoms with no persistent biomarker rise, after excluding STEMI/NSTEMI and non-cardiac causes.

firstLine: Treat as ACS pathway: aspirin loading unless contraindicated
secondLine: Second antiplatelet and anticoagulation per local protocol/senior plan
procedures: Urgent cardiology input for early invasive strategy in high-risk patients

monitoring: Secondary prevention: statin, BP/lipid/diabetes control, smoking cessation, cardiac rehab

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.dosing: Loading then maintenance as per ACS protocol.

content.prognosis: Higher short-term risk of MI compared with stable angina; prognosis improves with rapid ACS management.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Initiate ACS bundle promptly, obtain serial ECG/troponin, and escalate to seniors/cardiology early.
content.escalation: Immediate escalation for persistent pain, ECG changes, hypotension, arrhythmia, or rising biomarkers.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Do not miss STEMI/NSTEMI progression; reassess frequently and document timing of pain/ECGs/troponins.
